title: Design 4-to-2 Encoder Using Two 4x1 MUXs
description: Design a 4-to-2 encoder using two 4×1 MUXs and basic gates as required. Assume that at most one input is HIGH at a time. The encoder should generate the corresponding 2-bit binary code at its outputs. When all inputs are LOW, the output should be 00.
author: Tahmid, Rounak

requiredArchitecture.description: Use one 4×1 MUX to implement Y1 and another 4×1 MUX to implement Y0. Use D3 as S1 and D2 as S0 for both MUXs. Since at most one encoder input is HIGH at a time, the D2=D3=1 select condition is invalid and may be treated as a don't-care condition.

hints: Assume that at most one of D0, D1, D2 or D3 can be HIGH at a time.
The encoder equations are Y1 = D2 + D3 and Y0 = D1 + D3.
Use D3 as S1 and D2 as S0 for the select inputs of both 4×1 MUXs.
For the Y1 MUX, connect I0 to logic LOW (0), I1 and I2 to logic HIGH (1), and I3 can be tied to 0, 1, or left unused as a don't-care state.
For the Y0 MUX, connect I0 to D1, I1 to logic LOW (0), I2 to logic HIGH (1), and I3 can be tied to 0, 1, or left unused as a don't-care state.
The select condition D3D2 = 11 is invalid because only one encoder input may be HIGH at a time.
Connect the first MUX output to Y1 and the second MUX output to Y0.
Connect Y1 and Y0 to LED0 and LED1 respectively.
